values: A default sphere is placed at the origin of the 3D viewport in Blender.

• Switch to Sculpt Mode on the top-left menu
• Select 'Grab' brush from the toolbar
• Resize brush radius with 'F' hotkey shortcut
• Perform continuous mouse drags on the outer boundaries of the sphere
• Switch viewport orientation to Top View (Numpad 7) and Front View (Numpad 1)
The sphere is elongated vertically and flattened on the lateral sides to establish the basic proportions of a stylized skull.
The primary skull shape is established, but lacks jaw structure.

• Switch to Object Mode using 'Ctrl + Tab'
• Press 'Shift + D' to duplicate the skull object
• Press 'G' then 'Z' to translate the duplicate object downward along the global Z-axis
• Switch back to Sculpt Mode using 'Ctrl + Tab'
• Select 'Grab' brush and drag the lower region of the duplicate mesh
Main skull mesh and duplicated jaw mesh
A secondary, overlapping sphere is positioned below the skull and deformed to serve as the structural block for the jaw.
Two separate, rough spheres representing the skull and the jaw overlap with unrefined transitions.

• Press 'Alt + Q' to switch active focus between the skull and duplicated jaw meshes in Sculpt Mode
• Rotate viewport to Side View (Numpad 3)
• Use 'Grab' brush to pull the chin forward and push the throat area backward
• Hold 'Shift' to activate the Smooth brush on the mesh boundaries
Overlapping skull and jaw blockout meshes
The chin is projected forward and the jawline angle is refined to establish a clear profile silhouette.
The facial area is a smooth curve without planar definition for the eyes, brow, or temples.

• Press 'Alt + Q' to toggle active focus back to the skull mesh
• Use 'Grab' brush with medium radius to push the eye socket region backward
• Press 'Ctrl + Z' to undo an accidental stroke at 00:49
• Use 'Crease' or 'Draw Sharp' brush to define the border of the temple planes
• Hold 'Shift' to smooth the transitions across the forehead planes
Frontal region of the skull mesh
Eye socket recesses are formed, the brow ridge is defined, and flat temple planes are established on the forehead.
Head and jaw structures are roughly blocked out but their relative scale and connection points need refinement.

• Rotate viewport around the model to inspect symmetry and proportions
• Press 'Alt + Q' to alternate active objects and adjust relative positions
• Hold 'Shift' to smooth out neck connection zones
The overall volume distribution of the head blockout is balanced, showing a correct spatial relationship from different viewing angles.
The face has blocked-out eye sockets and cheeks but lacks a nose structure.

• Switch to Object Mode and press 'Shift + A' -> Mesh -> UV Sphere
• Scale ('S') the sphere down and translate ('G') it to the center of the face
• Switch to Edit Mode and select vertices on the front of the sphere
• Enable 'Proportional Editing' ('O' key) and translate the vertices forward along the Y-axis
Nose sphere mesh placed on the face
A small sphere is added and elongated forward, establishing the initial volume and bridge of the nose.
A primitive elongated sphere sits on the face representing the rough nose bridge.

• Switch viewport to Side View (Numpad 3)
• Translate selected bottom vertices of the nose mesh downward in Edit Mode
• Switch to Sculpt Mode and apply 'Grab' brush on the nose tip and nostrils
• Press 'Alt + Q' to quickly check nose integration against the cheeks
The nose blockout is refined to show a flat front plane, stylized tip, and defined nostril shapes.
The head blockout has facial features but no ear structures.

• In Object Mode, press 'Shift + A' -> Mesh -> Cylinder
• Scale ('S') the cylinder down and flatten it along one axis
• Rotate ('R') and position ('G') the flattened cylinder on the side of the head
• Add a loop cut in Edit Mode ('Ctrl + R') and scale the outer edges to taper the ear
A flattened, rotated cylinder is placed on the side of the head, representing the basic mass and orientation of the ear.
The head elements are blocked out, but the head is floating with no neck support.

• In Object Mode, press 'Shift + A' -> Mesh -> Cylinder
• Scale ('S') and position ('G') the cylinder beneath the jaw base
• In Edit Mode, select the bottom vertex loop and scale ('S') it outward
• Add a loop cut ('Ctrl + R') in the middle of the cylinder to allow for curvature
A flared cylinder is created and aligned, connecting the base of the skull/jaw to the upper collarbone plane.
The head and neck are blocked out, but there is no body structure.

• Press 'Shift + A' -> Mesh -> UV Sphere (or Round Cube)
• Translate ('G') the sphere down along the Z-axis and scale ('S') it up
• Switch to Sculpt Mode and select 'Grab' brush
• Drag the sides of the sphere to pull out the shoulders and flatten the front of the chest
A large, flattened chest mass is generated below the neck, establishing the width of the shoulders and rib cage.
The upper torso blockout is active, but lacks waist and pelvic masses.

• In Object Mode, duplicate ('Shift + D') or add a primitive mesh
• Scale ('S') and translate ('G') it below the rib cage chest mesh
• In Sculpt Mode, use 'Grab' brush to deform the lower mass into a wedge shape matching the pelvic tilt
An overlapping pelvic wedge is positioned below the rib cage, establishing the core gesture of the lower torso.
Multiple separate, intersecting blockout meshes (torso, shoulders, neck) exist as individual objects with visible, hard intersections.

• Select multiple overlapping meshes sequentially (visualized by orange outline shifts on screen)
• Trigger a merge/join operation (command name: unknown)
• Trigger a remeshing operation, which instantly converts the intersecting geometry into a single unified polygon grid (settings and grid resolution: unknown)
• Use a smoothing tool (brush name and hotkey: unknown; cursor turns blue/cyan) to paint over the seam lines at the neck and shoulder joints
Intersections of the neck, shoulders, and chest meshes
The distinct, intersecting primitive shapes are fused into a single watertight mesh with smooth, continuous surface transitions.
The merged torso is a smooth, amorphous shape without chest definition or skeletal landmarks.

• Select a sculptural brush (brush name and hotkey: unknown; cursor is circular yellow with a flat-strip profile effect)
• Draw horizontal strokes across the upper chest to pull out a raised bone ridge
• Draw downward-curving strokes to carve the borders of the pectoral muscles
• Orbit the viewport to a low camera angle looking upward at the chest (interaction method: unknown)
Clavicle and pectoral muscle areas on the upper torso
Stylized planar forms are established, defining the collarbone line and chest musculature.
The arm blockout terminates in a simplified, flat cube representing the hand mass, with no fingers.

• Switch to Edit Mode (indicated by wireframe and mesh vertex display overlays)
• Select specific polygons on the front face of the hand block
• Trigger repeated extrusion operations (hotkey: unknown) to create segmented finger lengths
• Apply scaling and rotation adjustments (tool or hotkey: unknown) on the joint loops to create a natural, slightly curved finger pose
The blocky hand structure is developed into four distinct fingers with basic joint subdivisions.
The character sculpt is fully symmetrical along the X-axis (standard A-pose).

• Deactivate the Symmetry (X) toggle on the interface (icon status changes to off)
• Select a deformation brush (brush name and hotkey: unknown; cursor is a large yellow circle)
• Drag the hip mass upward on one side and pull the opposite shoulder downward
• Rotate the viewport 360 degrees around the character to inspect the resulting weight-bearing tilt
The rigid symmetry of the pose is broken, introducing a stylized contrapposto pose with a tilted pelvis and offset shoulder line.
The character body blockout modeling is complete, showing refined shapes and muscles.

• Select the entire character mesh in Object Mode (highlighted with an orange selection boundary)
• Set viewport shading to Flat or Matcap mode (wireframe lines and textures are disabled, leaving a solid shaded silhouette on screen)
• Initiate a continuous orbit rotation around the character model (interaction method: unknown)
• Zoom the viewport camera out to assess the entire character's profile against the background
The final model's negative space, outline silhouette, and volumetric proportions are audited from all angles.
